SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: MY EXTENDED FAMILY
Subject: ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION · Grade: PP2
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
My extended family helps you succeed in ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

KEY FACTS: MY EXTENDED FAMILY
Good citizens follow rules, respect others, and care for shared places.
Kenyan examples: lining up, keeping the compound clean, telling the truth, helping a classmate.
Rights come with responsibilities.

PART 1: Recognise the alphabet (fat'ha, kasra, dhumm

What this means
In this part you learn to recognise the alphabet (fat'ha, kasra, dhumm. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: recognise the alphabet (fat'ha, kasra, dhumm.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Locate: Connect “My extended family” to a real place or group in Kenya (school, market, county office, home).

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can recognise the alphabet (fat'ha, kasra, dhumm. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Name correctly three • Learners are guided to use digital (

What this means
In this part you learn to name correctly three • Learners are guided to use digital (. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: name correctly three • Learners are guided to use digital (.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Explain: Give one cause and one effect linked to My extended family.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can name correctly three • Learners are guided to use digital (. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what My extended family is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Kenyan examples: lining up, keeping the compound clean, telling the truth, helping a classmate.

Example 2: Give one cause and one effect linked to My extended family. (skill: name correctly three • Learners are guided to use digital ()

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach My extended family to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: recognise the alphabet (fat'ha, kasra, dhumm.
3. Practise this skill: name correctly three • Learners are guided to use digital (.
4. Make one local Kenya example of My extended family from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for My extended family: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a PP2 learner study My extended family?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what My extended family means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: recognise the alphabet (fat'ha, kasra, dhumm.
5. Be able to: name correctly three • Learners are guided to use digital (.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.
